Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE full-screen landscape 16:10 game interface mockup for "theseus", a browser space-trading game. This is a practical playable GAME SCREEN with beautifully composed simple low-poly geometry, not a cinematic concept illustration, not a presentation slide or web dashboard.
Art direction: human civilizations of uneven technological development; old working equipment modernized over generations. Stanislaw Lem's everyday spacefaring, competent imperfect humans, quiet institutional absurdity. Atomic-era cream enamel, petrol teal machinery, restrained oxblood, mustard brass details, lavender shadows on a near-black violet background. Think simple independent strategy game, visible faceted forms and broad flat materials. Clean geometrical shadows make every shape readable. NO realistic wear textures, tiny greebles, photorealism, elaborate illustrations, lens effects, depth of field, cartoon faces, ornate UI, holograms. Wear is one or two large paint patches. Machines should look useful and locally coherent, not random steampunk. No aliens.
Shared UI: top slim bar at y=0..7%, "theseus / lem station" left; "credits 12,480" and "hold 6/24" right. Left slim navigation strip with five simple outlined icons and lowercase labels "port", "rig", "market", "comms", "map"; active section amber. Main scene covers most remaining space. Minimal dark violet panels, fine muted lavender keylines, warm ivory text, amber primary buttons. Titles rounded sans medium/bold, data and small labels readable monospace. All lettering lowercase. Keep screen text sparse and accurate. Plenty of negative space. At bottom right, incorporate a modest technical drawing title block or panel with compact metadata, echoing old engineering drawings. No browser chrome. Crisp final screenshot, professionally aligned, no excessive HUD widgets.

Active view: port. The main scene is a SIMPLE floating orbital station above a faint blueprint grid in purple space. Orthographic isometric, entire station visible, large recognizable masses, at most about 60 chunky objects. An old ivory cylindrical observatory forms the core, one enormous faceted listening dish on a plain oxblood support tower, several later teal and mustard cargo blocks, a small repaired docking arm and a single burgundy/cream courier. NO ground slab/pedestal. A tiny warm canteen window suggests life. Honest constructible low-poly primitive geometry.
Three sparse interactive facility labels anchored to objects: "market hall", "repair berth", "signals office". Repair berth selected with thin amber outline; one small contextual panel on right says "repair berth", "berth 04 available", and amber button "enter rigging". Bottom right technical title block: "lem station", "orbital observatory / trading port", "sol system". Small muted line below the station: "listening array / no confirmed contact". Make navigation and spatial facility selection obvious. Station silhouette and amber berth selection dominate, not text.
